text: The Patriots face a significant challenge heading into Sunday's 1 PM ET home opener against the Steelers at Gillette Stadium, as wide receiver A.J. Brown has been placed on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain suffered in Week 1, sidelining him for at least four games and forcing the offense to find new weapons while Drake Maye looks to bounce back in his second NFL start. Coach Mike Vrabel will need to address both the injury contingencies and roster adjustments in what figures to be a crucial game for momentum, while off the field, owner Robert Kraft demonstrated the organization's values by having rapper Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming Gillette Stadium shows, citing concerns over antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that he felt would be offensive to the Jewish community. On a more uplifting note, Maye and his wife Ann Michael made headlines for their generosity to the Providence community, funding the Amazon classroom wish lists for more than 50 teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School—a reminder that despite the football challenges ahead, there's plenty to admire about the character of this team's roster.
